verifiedBy: npm dist-tags.latest on registry.npmjs.org (0.6.0, published 2026-10-22) cross-read against the git tag of the same version (`git show v0.6.0:cmd/litespm/main.go` → parseInstallFlags). The release that tag cut is the one the npm wrapper downloads its binary from.
_readme: What a reader actually installs. `npx --yes litespm@latest` resolves to this
version, so these are the only install flags the site may publish — the
flags a reader's binary accepts is a property of npm, not of this working
tree. That distinction is what let the site publish `--agent` and
`--all-detected` while npm still served 0.4.1, which rejected both: the
site printed a command whose answer was `unknown flag`.
This file recorded 0.4.1 and its eight flags from 2026-10-22 until the
0.6.0 release landed that evening, which is what let the site be honest
in between. Keep it in step with npm: scripts/check-install-command.mjs
asks the registry which version `latest` is (falling back to this file
offline) and fails when they disagree, so a publish cannot leave this
snapshot — and therefore the site — behind.
